summary:
**ASTRA – Intelligent Astronaut Health Monitoring Ecosystem**

ASTRA is an intelligent astronaut health-monitoring ecosystem designed to support crew health and mission awareness during spaceflight. It brings together three connected interfaces: an Astronaut Health Profile, a Ground Control Dashboard, and a VR-based Digital Twin with a Helmet HUD.

ASTRA organizes vital health telemetry, including heart rate, blood pressure, blood oxygen, respiration, temperature, sleep, and radiation exposure. Its analytical approach compares readings with each astronaut’s personal baseline, assesses signal quality, and uses AI-assisted analysis to identify unusual health trends.

The system also explores gravity-adaptive health baselines for different environments, including Earth, the Moon, Mars, and deep space, alongside delay-tolerant telemetry to address communication challenges between astronauts and Earth.

ASTRA addresses the challenge of monitoring human health in extreme space environments by connecting individual health data, intelligent analysis, mission control, and immersive visualization in one ecosystem.

Its importance lies in supporting earlier awareness of potential health changes, improving access to meaningful health information, and helping advance safer, more informed human space exploration.
details:
Project Details — ASTRA

How it works

ASTRA is an integrated astronaut health-monitoring ecosystem that connects three main interfaces: an individual Astronaut Health Dashboard, a Ground Control Dashboard, and a 3D VR Digital Twin with a Helmet HUD.

The system organizes astronaut health telemetry, including heart rate, blood pressure, blood oxygen (SpO₂), respiration, core temperature, sleep, HRV, and radiation exposure. It compares health readings with individual baseline values, evaluates signal quality to identify potentially unreliable measurements caused by motion artifacts, and supports AI-assisted analysis of unusual health trends.

The Ground Control interface provides a shared view of crew health information, while the VR Helmet HUD presents relevant telemetry in an immersive 3D mission environment.

Benefits and Intended Impact

ASTRA aims to improve astronaut health awareness by bringing important health information into one connected ecosystem. It helps make changes in health trends easier to identify, supports communication between onboard systems and ground control, and provides a more intuitive way to understand complex telemetry during missions.

Its intended impact is to contribute to safer, better-informed long-duration space missions, where continuous health awareness and communication challenges are critical.

Tools and Technologies

We developed the web-based system using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with Vite as the development environment and Three.js/WebGL for 3D visualization and the VR-style Helmet HUD. The project was developed and tested using laptop-based software tools, without requiring dedicated VR hardware. AI-assisted development tools supported parts of the development workflow.

Creativity and Engineering Considerations

ASTRA goes beyond displaying isolated vital signs by combining individual baseline monitoring, a proposed Gravity-Adaptive Baseline Calibration (G-ABC) approach, synchronized 3D visualization, and delay-tolerant telemetry concepts.

Our team considered the physiological challenges of different gravity environments, communication delays, motion-related signal errors, data reliability, interface usability, and the distinction between verified research data and simulated demonstration scenarios. These considerations shaped ASTRA as a connected, space-focused health-monitoring concept rather than a conventional health dashboard.
